implement.approach: Started from BASE_SHA f250acd7 on branch devin/pp/w07-05/impl-r3. Reused the sound parts of r2 (membershipState.ts module, Paywall/Settings wiring, paywallCopy hero mapping) but re-derived the state machine so every displayed state is bound to a server answer: (1) accessStore now stores canonicalBilling from /v1/billing/sync and a fulfilmentVerdict bound to the device's own pending id/attempt/transaction; publishAccess/initialize/direct-access loads clear fulfilmentVerdict as soon as a server access answer grants premium (A1: a refund verdict for purchase #1 can never describe a later lapse). (2) 'expired' is derived ONLY from a bound expired/refunded verdict or a billing.purchase_settled error — never from a stale premium billing horizon beside non-premium access; a lapsed member whose server truth is premium=false is deterministically 'free' after access refresh, billing sync and cold start (A2). Grace ('renewal unconfirmed') requires access.premium=true plus a premium billing horizon in the past. (3) Grace copy branches on reconciliationStatus: when 'unavailable' it says the server could not be reached to re-verify since the last verified horizon, never that the server 'still reports' anything (A3). Manage subscription (Linking.openURL('https://apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions'), with a non-fatal brand notice on failure) is shown in Settings and Paywall only when the server attached a premium expiry horizon — lifetime/non-consumable access (expiresAt null) never exposes it. Pending/HOLD states withhold plans, prices and purchase CTAs and offer 'Retry verification' (server verifyPending, not StoreKit). Prices are only ever store-returned plan.price. Regression suite committed first (7ad897dd), implementation second (706a2435), plus a follow-up (2b257a06) making the premium-horizon read null-safe (`billing?.premium`) so an untouched workflow test fixture that seeds the store without canonicalBilling keeps passing.

implement.approach: Regression test first (commit 01476b94), then the fix in two commits (529123a8 implementation, 6dc61a4d grace copy). Root cause on the prior candidate (2b257a06, apps/mobile/src/state/accessStore.ts): `publishAccess()` wrote `canonicalAccess` but never touched `canonicalBilling`, so a `/v1/billing/sync` horizon survived a non-premium `GET /v1/me/access` answer and re-attached to a later premium answer; `describeMembershipState` (membershipState.ts:209) then read `billing.premium && expiresAt` and produced 'Pro active through Mar 1, 2027' + manageSubscription:true where a cold start on the same server state gives 'Pro active' / null / false. Fix: `billingSnapshotAfterAccess(access, billing, receivedAtMs)` (membershipState.ts) returns the held billing snapshot only when access.premium && billing.premium and the horizon (if any) is still ahead of the receipt clock; accessStore's `VerifiedAccess` gained `billingSynced` — access-only loads (`loadAccess`, initialize/reconcile publication) run the snapshot through `publishedBilling()`/`supersededBilling()` and drop it otherwise, while sync answers keep the server's billing verbatim (`verifyBackend` sets `canonicalBilling: result.billing`). Result: non-premium answer ⇒ canonicalBilling null; later premium answer without a new sync ⇒ identical to cold start; premium answer received past the horizon ⇒ 'Pro active' with no horizon until a new sync; a valid future horizon and lifetime (horizon-less) billing are preserved. Grace copy (the adversary's third case) no longer asserts a server negative the client cannot know ('has not re-verified a renewal yet'); it states only what this app has loaded ('Pro access on this account is granted as of the last server check, and this app has not loaded a newer membership period yet'; label 'Pro active · renewal not yet loaded'). Also carried from r3 with fixes: expired/refunded copy keeps the server free-rating ledger visible; no membership copy asserts a charging guarantee; Manage subscription opens https://apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions only while the server reports a subscription horizon (never for lifetime, pending, HOLD, expired or free).
out_of_scope_files: apps/mobile/src/state/accessStore.ts — the only shipping owner of canonicalAccess/canonicalBilling/pendingFulfilment; inside the `mobile-billing` serial group this package holds. Minimal wiring: `canonicalBilling` + `fulfilmentVerdict` slices, `selectMembershipState` selector, `VerifiedAccess.billingSynced` flag, and `publishedBilling()`/`supersededBilling()` (call `billingSnapshotAfterAccess` from apps/mobile/src/billing/membershipState.ts) on every access-only publication so a stale horizon cannot survive a non-premium answer or re-attach to a later premium grant.

Not changed: persisting a settled terminal verdict across launches would require a new durable journal record in apps/mobile/src/billing/pendingFulfilment.ts with an open question of retention (how long an old refund/expiry should keep labelling an account), and after relaunch the shown state is the server's current truth (non-premium, free ratings from the ledger), not an invented one.

Grace between answers is clock-based (device `nowMs` vs the last synced horizon); the store invalidates the snapshot at receipt time with Date.now(). A device clock jumped far ahead shows grace until the next access answer, which (received 'past' the horizon on that clock) drops the horizon to plain 'Pro active' until a new sync — never expired, never a purchase offer (pinned by the boundary/clock-rollback tests).

Manage subscription uses Linking.openURL on the App Store subscriptions URL; Apple runtime behaviour (deep-link into Settings › Subscriptions) is INFERRED from the URL contract, not verified here (Linux-only checks). Failure to open shows a notice and never changes membership (tested).
